title: Rating the Pitch, Not the Product: User Evaluations of LLMs Reflect Expectations More Than Performance
abstract: arXiv:2607.05113v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Imagine two users interact with the same LLM. One has been told it is the cutting-edge flagship model; the other, an older, weaker model. They walk away with markedly different ratings of its usefulness and intelligence, yet they used the same model. In a controlled study, 162 participants each used one of six LLMs from two families across three collaborative tasks, after first viewing a landing page that matched, overstated, or understated their model's true capability. This pre-interaction framing shifted user opinions and interaction behavior while task performance did not. Oversold users rated the model more favorably and used more directive prompting, while Undersold users wrote longer, more collaborative prompts. The quality of what users and the model produced together depended only on the model's true capability, not on what users were told. translated_title: 评分的是宣传，而非产品：用户对大语言模型的评价更多反映预期而非实际表现
translated_abstract: 想象两位用户与同一个大语言模型互动。一位被告知这是最尖端的旗舰模型；另一位则被告知这是一个较旧、较弱的模型。他们对模型有用性和智能程度的评价截然不同，然而他们使用的其实是同一个模型。在一项对照研究中，162名参与者分别使用了来自两个系列的六种大语言模型中的一种，完成三项协作任务，在此之前他们首先查看了一个与模型真实能力相符、夸大或贬低模型能力的落地页。这种交互前的框架设定改变了用户的观点和交互行为，但任务表现并未因此改变。被过度宣传的用户对模型评价更高，并使用更多指令性提示；被低估的用户则编写更长、更具协作性的提示。用户与模型共同产出的质量仅取决于模型的真实能力，而不取决于用户被告知的内容。参与者在使用后对模型印象的变化，通过两种印象衡量维度进行测量……
tldr: 该研究通过对照实验发现，用户对大语言模型的评价主要受交互前宣传预期的影响而非实际表现，但人机协作产出的质量只取决于模型的真实能力。
en_tdlr: Through a controlled experiment, this study shows that user evaluations of LLMs are driven mainly by pre-interaction framing and expectations rather than actual performance, while the quality of human-AI collaborative output depends solely on the model's true capability.
